summary.text: Son of Phaenops (`phaenops-trojan`), well beloved with his brother Xanthus, whom mighty Diomedes slew when their father was fordone with grievous old age and begat no other son — distinct from Thoön whom Agamemnon slew in *Iliad* 11.

story.text: After slaying Polyidus and his brother, sons of the dream-reader Eurydamas, Diomedes went on after Xanthus and Thoön, sons twain of Phaenops, and both well beloved. There Diomedes slew them and bereft them of dear life, both the twain; but for the father he left lamentation and grievous sorrow.
